about: Grade 5 wording for the spoken step explanations (stepVoice in app.config.json). Grades 1-4 keep the builder's own lines, which were written for six-year-olds: 'A word is a picture you can say', 'follow the words with your finger', 'colour it, draw it, act it out'. Each entry is the four parts explain() takes: calm, friendly, watch, go. Written 2026-09-11.

explain: Your teacher recorded this lesson to open the unit.
Watch it to the end.
Turn the captions on if you want to read along.
You can watch it again at any time.
Keep a notebook open.
Write down one idea you want to remember.
Press play.
These words share one spelling pattern.
You will hear a word.
Listen to the end of it, then tap the word you heard.
Words with the same pattern can look almost alike.
Check every letter before you tap.
Press Hear it again whenever you need to.
These are the new words for this unit.
Read the word and what it means.
Say it out loud, then press Next word.
A word you have said is easier to remember than one you have only read.
Press Hear it to check how it sounds, then say it again.
Match each picture to its word.
Look at the picture and name what it shows.
Then find that word and tap it.
Two words can begin the same way.
Read to the end of the word before you tap.
Name it first, then tap it.
Speaking is part of learning a language.
Press the speaker to hear the line.
Then say it yourself, out loud, with a partner or on your own.
Nothing on this page listens to you or marks you.
Tick a line when you have said it clearly.
Your turn. Out loud.
English has patterns, and a pattern is something you can reuse.
The gold line is the pattern.
Learn it, and you can build many sentences of your own.
Read the Watch out box.
It shows the mistake most learners make with this pattern.
Press Hear it, read it once more, then press Next.
These are this unit's speaking tasks.
Choose one. Read it, or press Listen.
Do it out loud, with a partner, an adult or on your own.
Nothing on this page is listening to you.
Tick a task when you have done it.
Pick a task and talk.
This is the reading the unit is built around.
Pick one and press Read.
Press Listen and follow the words as you hear them.
Press Next page when you are ready.
The next step asks about the story.
You can come back and read it again at any time.
Pick one and press Listen.
These are tasks you do away from the screen.
Read one, or press Listen.
Do it in your notebook, out loud or with a partner.
Then come back and tick it.
Nothing here is marked.
Press How did I do to see what a finished task looks like.
Pick one and start.
